documents.title: Interim Policy Prohibiting Entering Confidential Information into Generative AI
documents.stance_why: The document bans one thing: "Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools". Within what it governs (data entry by all students, faculty and staff) that is a prohibition; it says nothing on coursework use, so it does not set a course-level stance.
documents.summary: An interim IT policy, sponsored by the CIO and CISO, that bans entering confidential institutional, employee or student data into generative AI tools and points to a list of authorized tools. It says nothing about AI in coursework and is meant to be folded into a revised data policy.

units.why: The purpose section warns that "information entered into a generative AI tool immediately becomes part of the generative AI's information database", a fact explaining why the rule exists. Coded as data protection (P50) because the point is that tools retain prompts; informs, general phase.
units.anchor: immediately becomes part of the generative AI’s information database

units.why: "entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public" states the risk consequence of entering data; it is rationale for the data rule, so P50 (protect personal data), informs.
units.anchor: entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public

units.why: The policy is put in place "on an interim basis" while "a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed", marking it as provisional and to be revised: P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: on an interim basis in order to deal with immediate risks of unintended disclosure
units.policy: This policy is interim and is in place while a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed.

units.why: The policy states "We intend to integrate language related to generative AI usage" into the revised Data Classification and Usage Policy, a plan to fold AI language into an existing policy. P54 fits (planned revision); P77 does not fit as well because it is not a compliance rule.
units.anchor: We intend to integrate language related to generative AI usage into that revised policy.

units.why: The text says the policy comes from "collaboratively reviewing WPI's Data Classification and Usage Policy", describing the process by which the guidance was developed, so P84.
units.anchor: collaboratively reviewing WPI’s Data Classification and Usage Policy

units.why: "This Policy applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI" sets the scope and who is bound; scope statement fits P61 (define the policy's scope).
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI.
units.fit_note: Sets who the policy binds rather than defining AI.

units.why: The definition of "Confidential Information" (institutional, employee and student data, e.g. SSNs, FERPA records) sets what the ban covers: scope definition, P61, with the content being data types.
units.anchor: confidential WPI institutional data, confidential WPI employee data, and WPI student data
units.policy: Confidential Information means confidential WPI institutional data, confidential WPI employee data, and WPI student data that is not publicly available and should not be released publicly.
units.fit_note: Defines the data category the AI ban covers, not AI itself.

units.why: The bullet list names protected data types ("Student records protected by FERPA", "Health care information protected under HIPAA"), which specifies what is covered; the primary role is scope definition (P61).
units.policy: Confidential Information includes social security numbers, financial account information, passwords, driver's license numbers, HIPAA-protected health care information, human resources and personnel information, FERPA-protected student records, and gift and donor information.
units.fit_note: A list of data categories rather than a definition of AI.

units.why: "Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools" is a direct ban on a use, binding everyone, so must-not. It is the core data-protection rule (P50) rather than P20 because it concerns confidential data, not assignment specs or code.
units.anchor: Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Google Gemini, etc.).

units.why: "A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase" points users to an institutionally authorized tool list, so P92 (use approved tools).
units.anchor: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase
units.policy: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase or by contacting the ITS Service Desk.
units.fit_note: Does not say authorized tools must be used; it only points to the list.

units.why: "you should seek guidance from your manager, Department Head or WPI's Information Technology Services ... before entering information in a generative AI tool" tells unsure users to ask first, so P10 (ask before using).
units.anchor: you should seek guidance from your manager, Department Head or WPI’s Information Technology Services
units.policy: Anyone with questions or concerns should seek guidance from their manager, Department Head or Information Technology Services before entering information in a generative AI tool.
units.fit_note: Addressed to employees and students generally, about data entry, not coursework permissions.

units.why: The footer names the "Policy Sponsor: Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer" and responsible department, identifying who owns the policy: P80.
units.anchor: Policy Sponsor: Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer
units.policy: The policy sponsors are the Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer; the responsible department is Information Technology.

units.why: The effective-date line records "Presidential Approval" on December 4, 2023 and later extensions of the interim period, stating when and by whom the policy was adopted and extended: P84.
units.anchor: Effective Date of First Interim Policy (i.e., date of Presidential Approval): December 4, 2023
units.policy: The first interim policy took effect on December 4, 2023 with Presidential Approval, and the interim period has been extended with Presidential Approval.

notes: Only one included document: a thin data-protection policy with no coursework AI content. The effective-date line has inconsistent dates (Sept. 25, 2026 - Mar. 26, 2026) and the inconsistency was not coded.
